race.name: CRC 506 Gran Fondo Costa Rica
race.tagline: 141.4 km and 841 m on Costa Rica's exposed Pacific coast — a UCI Gran Fondo World Series qualifier from Jacó to Quepos and back.

vitals.location: Jacó, Garabito, Puntarenas Province, Costa Rica
vitals.date_specific: September 13, 2026 (Sunday; rescheduled from June 7 due to severe-weather risk)
vitals.start_format: Gran Fondo controlled start at 6:00am from the Centro Cívico por la Paz in Garabito, followed by the timed rolling start on Ruta 34
vitals.registration: Reopened June 22 through the organizer's 2026 site after the September rescheduling
vitals.entry_fee: Not specified; register at official site
vitals.feed_zones: Organizer technical guide stations at km 24.4, 53.3, 72, 88, and 117.3, with food and drink in signed feed zones.
vitals.cutoff_time: Gran Fondo riders must reach the km 72 control at the Route 34 / Route 235 junction by 9:30am.

climate.description: Warm, humid tropical conditions on an exposed Pacific coast during Costa Rica's September rainy season.
challenges: Heat and high humidity from the early-morning start
September rain and storm risk on the Pacific coast
Exposed coastal wind on the return from Quepos

terrain.surface: Paved Ruta 34 out-and-back between Jacó and Quepos. The 141.4 km course gains 841 m, so sustained speed, wind exposure, heat management, and group position matter more than long climbing.
features: 4.6 km controlled rollout from Jacó before the timed start
Long exposed Ruta 34 coastal sectors through Esterillos and Parrita
Quepos circuit and turnaround near km 72
Five organizer feed points across the 141.4 km Gran Fondo

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Migrated from gravel-race-automation. Original score: 70. adventure dimension dropped, road_surface added. Score recalculated: 66.

course_description.character: The Gran Fondo starts at 6:00am with a 4.6 km controlled rollout from Jacó, then follows Ruta 34 through Esterillos and Parrita to a Quepos circuit before returning to Jacó. Its 141.4 km and 841 m profile is flattish, but the exposed coast, heat, rain risk, and repeated group accelerations keep it from being easy. The current technical guide lists a separate 69.8 km Medio Fondo starting near Quepos at 7:30am.
course_description.signature_challenge: Holding the right group and a sustainable cooling and fueling plan through the Quepos turnaround, then racing the exposed return to Jacó.
suffering_zones: Ruta 34 exposure after the controlled rollout
Quepos circuit and km 72 time control
Headwind and heat accumulation on the return through Parrita and Esterillos

logistics.transport: Nearest major airport: Juan Santamaría (SJO). Gran Fondo start and finish: Centro Cívico por la Paz, Garabito, Jacó. Medio Fondo start: Route 34 / Route 235 junction near Quepos; finish in Jacó.

history.origin_story: Founded in 2023 as a Costa Rican UCI Gran Fondo World Series qualifier. The first edition drew roughly 700 riders from San José to Puntarenas; the event later moved to the Jacó–Quepos–Jacó coast route. The June 7, 2026 edition was postponed for severe-weather risk and rescheduled to September 13, 2026.

biased_opinion.summary: This is a speed-oriented UCI age-group qualifier rather than a mountain gran fondo: 141.4 km, 841 m, a controlled rollout, and long paved coastal sectors where the useful skill is staying economical in the right group. The Pacific setting is real, but so are heat, humidity, exposed wind, and September storm risk.
strengths: UCI Gran Fondo World Series qualification target for age-group racers
A fast 141.4 km coastal course with five organizer feed points and neutral mechanical support
Jacó start and finish simplify race-day logistics
weaknesses: September sits in the Pacific rainy season, and the original June date was already postponed for severe-weather risk
The flattish out-and-back can become tactically dependent on wind and group position
The organizer's rescheduled landing page and original technical guide must be read together because the PDF still carries the superseded June date
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A legitimate UCI qualifier for riders who want to race 141.4 fast coastal kilometres and can manage heat, wind, and group dynamics better than the next age-group pack.

final_verdict.one_liner: 141.4 km of fast Pacific-coast group racing, with heat and wind doing more selection than the 841 m of climbing.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you want a UCI age-group qualification target on a fast tropical road course. Skip if mountain climbing is the reason you enter a gran fondo or if September storm risk makes travel uncertainty unacceptable.

eligibility.notes: The organizer's current 2026 landing page confirms Sunday September 13 after the June 7 postponement and says registration reopened June 22. The organizer's English technical guide still carries the superseded June date, so it is used only for the unchanged course and operations: 141.4 km Gran Fondo, 69.8 km Medio Fondo, 6:00am controlled Gran Fondo start, five feed points, and the km 72 / 9:30am control. The rescheduled race qualifies riders for the 2027 UCI Gran Fondo World Championships in France.
